definition: Prompting is the use of embedded cues or questions within instructional support to guide learners during a cognitively demanding task such as experimentation. In this context, it is treated as a component of incremental scaffolds that may add cognitive and affective support beyond giving sample solutions alone.

reasons: The definition adds specifics not stated in the packet, such as prompting being “embedded cues or questions” and a general instructional-support mechanism for guiding learners.

“Sample solutions alone” and the claim that prompting adds “cognitive and affective support” are only partially supported; the packet says the study examined added value of prompting within incremental scaffolds versus sample solutions, but does not define prompting that broadly.

The packet does not explicitly define “prompting” as “embedded cues or questions,” only that the study compared “incremental scaffolds with embedded prompts” versus sample solutions without prompting.
